chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Safwan, from Isḥaq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū al-Ḥasan al-Awwal (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a pregnant woman who is divorced with a divorce that does not become effective until she marries another husband. He said: Yes. I said: Did you not tell me: If he has intercourse with her, it is not permissible for him to divorce her? He said: Indeed, divorce is not valid except during a period of purity in which intercourse has not occurred, and a pregnancy that has become evident; and in this case, her pregnancy has become evident.

key_terms.طُهْرٌ قَدْ بَانَ: Period of purity in which intercourse has not occurred

ai.seo_question: When does a divorce become effective for a pregnant woman in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Istibsar, Imam al-Riḍā (peace be upon him) clarifies the validity of divorce for a pregnant woman, resolving an apparent contradiction in his previous statements by distinguishing between pregnancies that are not yet evident and those that are clearly established. He asserts that while divorce generally requires a period of purity (ṭuhr) where the pregnancy is not yet obvious, once the pregnancy is evident, the divorce is valid immediately. This ruling underscores the importance of physical evidence in determining the timing of legal actions in Shia jurisprudence.
